record.title: Task detail role-specific lifecycle controls and feedback
record.description: The Work required student submission and assigned-mentor review, correction and completion, but the cited detail frames showed a generic upload/Submit path without role distinction or review and outcome states. The human accepted role-specific student and assigned-mentor flows and the necessary desktop/mobile feedback in clarification 15ef4e45-31a4-4e93-8d66-63bdcdfe7969.
record.conclusion: Resolved by accepted human clarification: the student sees their own submission, versions, and status; only the assigned mentor selects a version to review, completes the activity or requests corrections with a reason; desktop and mobile frames show successful/failed submission, lateness, stale-version, and completed/read-only outcomes.
record.rationale: The exact clarification exchange is accepted. Requirements, frontend, and backend reviews incorporated it; the AFU records the settled behavior as AFU-RULE-002 through AFU-RULE-004 and AFU-AC-003.

record.title: Submission upload limits and failure outcome
record.description: The task detail showed file upload without product limits or failure behavior, while Work requires each new submission to create a retained version. The human accepted the proposed bounded, atomic submission policy in clarification 9970c26d-d463-4f30-87b0-4449d9a5ea8a.
record.conclusion: Resolved by accepted human clarification: maximum 5 files per submission; 10 MiB per file and 25 MiB total; allowed formats PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, PNG and JPEG. Unsupported/oversized, cancelled or interrupted submission creates no version, leaves prior versions unchanged, explains the reason and permits correction/retry.
record.rationale: The accepted exchange binds explicit count/size/format bounds and the outcome for failed or interrupted uploads, making the external input bounded and the version-creation result testable. AFU-RULE-005 and AFU-AC-004 carry this conclusion.

record.title: In-app notification read interaction
record.description: Work requires notification-read state to differ from conversation-read state, while the Figma initially omitted an inbox and per-notification read interaction. Human clarification 250d30b1-5b0e-4478-8a06-ac8db516bc7f accepted the interaction.
record.conclusion: Resolved by accepted clarification: the bell opens an in-app list, the badge counts unread notifications, and each notification has an explicit Mark as read action. That action updates only the notification; reading a conversation updates only the conversation. Desktop/mobile placement is flexible.
record.rationale: The accepted exchange settles the visible read flow. Requirements and frontend AFU elements AFU-RULE-006 and AFU-AC-005 preserve the independent states and per-item action.

record.title: Notification category switches do not identify their channel
record.description: The Work requires email opt-out not to disable in-app notifications. Figma presents four notification-category switches without identifying their channel. The human accepted the proposal that the four switches are email-only, with in-app notifications remaining on and no category-level in-app opt-outs.
record.conclusion: Resolved by accepted clarification: Message, Task Update, Task Deadline and Mentor Help switches control only email for their category. In-app notifications stay active in the inbox and cannot be opted out by category; disabling email does not disable the corresponding in-app notice.
record.rationale: The accepted human clarification 4da29b06-1b37-43e7-a898-8e2d9eb5d71c directly resolves the channel and category-preference choice. AFU-RULE-007 and AFU-AC-002 carry the outcome.
